headline: Thirty markets wear the city before the crest: Nike Basketball wins by making the team the vessel for each market's own codes, climate, calendar and makers.
thesis: Across all 30 briefs the same pattern repeats: fans buy the area code, the ward, the county gym or the borough first and the roster second, which is why the briefs expect the 404, 112, 313, 901 and 92-county lines to outsell player product in reset markets and to deepen it in contender markets. The 2026 talent reshuffle (LeBron James and Ball's moves are in the verified league calendar; Giannis to Miami, Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia, Ja Morant to Portland and Kawhi Leonard to Toronto are confirmed in the Oct 7 live-verified League Pulse) left roughly a third of the league selling a new face and another third selling no face at all, so the team, the uniform system Nike makes for every club and Nike's own archives (Penny, Carter's purple era, Converse, the AF1 'Uptown', Specter for eight heritage clubs) are the durable assets. Climate and calendar, not the standings, set the product mix: a deep-winter layering season from Boston and Philadelphia to Minnesota and Utah, a fog-and-rain shoulder layer in the Bay and Portland, an inverted heat calendar across the Sun Belt, and diaspora gift windows that run from Black Friday to Three Kings Day, Orthodox Christmas and Lunar New Year. Nike earns the right to sell those codes only by paying and crediting the people who own them, from Albina and Roxbury to Oak Cliff, Little Haiti and the West Side of San Antonio, and the Portland team should run that as one repeatable partner system across the league rather than 30 one-off capsules.

themes.title: The area code is the new jersey
themes.insight: In 20 briefs the most bankable non-player graphic is a local numbering or geography system: 404/678/770, 112 ZIPs, 216 vs 330, the 313, DC's eight wards and 202, New Orleans ward numerals, the 901, 416/905, 405/918/580, the Clippers' six codes, 612/651/218, 92 Indiana counties, the 407, the 916 and Phoenix's Avenues-and-Streets grid. Fans use these to say which side of a city or state they are from, which a skyline or mascot cannot do.
themes.implication: Build one league-wide 'Codes' template (numeral type, side-hit cap, kids tee, heavyweight hoodie under each market's tax line) that each market fills with its own codes and a local artist's lettering, so the format is centralized and the content stays local. Drop each market on its own numeral date, not in one window: 202 Day Feb 2, 216 Day Feb 16, 313 Day Mar 13, 404 Day Apr 4, 405 Day Apr 5, 407 Day Apr 7, 416 Day Apr 16, 504 Day May 4, 612 Day Jun 12, 901 Day Sep 1 and 916 Day Sep 16 (only 404 Day and 407 Day are planned in the briefs; confirm the others are recognized locally before treating them as holidays). Treat it as evergreen volume with the team mark as a secondary hit, which protects reset markets from roster swings.

themes.title: Winter is the real uniform: a deep-winter tier and a fog-and-rain shoulder tier
themes.insight: From Boston's nor'easters, the New York and Philadelphia winter and Chicago's lake wind to Detroit's seven-month outerwear season, Minnesota's skyway walk, Toronto's 'Winter Blackout', Utah's inversion and Denver's Front Range swings, the dossiers describe fans wearing a jersey over a hoodie under a shell from October to March (DC's season is shorter). The Bay's 50-degree fog nights and Portland's wet Big Dark are a different spec: a light, water-resistant shoulder layer rather than insulation.
themes.implication: Run a shared layer platform in two tiers, applied by metro so both New York teams share one: a deep-winter tier (heavyweight fleece, insulated shell, oversized jersey cut to fit over a hoodie, knit beanie) and a shoulder tier (packable shell, quarter-zip, light fleece) for the Bay and Portland. Finish each with the city's material story (Cream City brick, Hulett truss linings, Mill City flour-sack cream, inversion gray, fog gray, Rip City reflective), re-merchandise existing Storm-FIT and Therma-FIT now and land the hero shells for FW27.

themes.title: The Sun Belt runs an inverted calendar
themes.insight: In Miami, Orlando, Phoenix, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio and New Orleans the dossiers set the spec as ventilation, sun, 3 p.m. downpours and arena air-conditioning, and the outdoor season is the NBA's offseason; Los Angeles (both teams), Sacramento's triple-digit summers and humid Atlanta, Charlotte and Memphis run the same way. August back-to-school, timed to Texas and Florida tax-free weekends, is a top-three retail month there while the northern markets are at their annual low.
themes.implication: Make mesh, satin, linen-look and UPF shooting shirts the Sun Belt hero rather than a cut-down version of the winter line, add packable rain shells for Florida and the Gulf, and build an August youth pack (tee, mesh short, sub-$100 shoe) that ships before the tax-free weekends.

themes.title: The 2026 reshuffle turned return games into local tentpoles
themes.insight: Giannis (Milwaukee to Miami; first meeting Nov 18 in Miami and his return to Fiserv Forum on Jan 28), Jaylen Brown (Boston to Philadelphia; Jan 21 at TD Garden), Ja Morant (Memphis to Portland, traded June 29), Kawhi Leonard (Clippers to Toronto) and LaMelo Ball (Charlotte to Minnesota; Feb 15 in Charlotte) are all confirmed in the live-verified League Pulse, and LeBron's move to Philadelphia (Christmas at the Lakers; the Sixers' home opener against Cleveland, date to confirm) is in the verified calendar. Each left a jersey closet behind; the Portland-Memphis and Toronto-Clippers meetings and Leonard's Toronto home debut are not yet dated, and the briefs agree these nights sell gratitude and the city, never the departed star.
themes.implication: Give each departing market (Milwaukee, Boston, Memphis, the Clippers, Charlotte, Cleveland) an undated, player-free 'thank you, city' piece and a re-stitch or patch kit for jerseys fans already own (Milwaukee's Keep the Jersey, the Clippers' closet rework), and give each arriving market deep name-and-number stock at the opener with local pieces unlocked only by wins, as Philadelphia's 'Earn Philly' plan does. Lock any return-night drop only once the date is on the published schedule.

themes.title: Nike makes the jersey; someone else often owns the face
themes.insight: Edwards and Ball (Minnesota), Lillard (Portland), Trae Young (Washington), Haliburton (Indiana), Iverson, Embiid and Brown (Philadelphia) and Charlotte's new core sit outside Nike's athlete roster, Curry's next shoe deal is open, and rivals hold Clyde, Marathon Monday and the Celtics' practice facility. What Nike holds outright is the uniform system, Specter for eight heritage clubs (Celtics, Lakers, Warriors, Knicks, 76ers, Kings, Pistons, Hawks) and archive stories no rival can tell: Penny in Orlando and Memphis, Carter's purple era in Toronto, Converse in Boston, Philadelphia and Charlotte, and the AF1 'Uptown' in New York.
themes.implication: Plan these markets team-first and archive-first: whole-roster jersey walls, Specter and City Edition moments, and Nike-family heritage capsules (Penny pinstripes, purple dino, Converse dynasty-era high-tops) carry the story, with athlete-led product reserved for the Nike faces who do play there (Giannis, LeBron, Wembanyama, Booker, Tatum, Doncic and Converse-signed Gilgeous-Alexander; Flagg, by contrast, is a New Balance athlete, so Dallas is also a team-first market).

themes.title: Holiday is plural: the gift season runs to Three Kings, Orthodox Christmas and Lunar New Year
themes.insight: The richest gifting calendars in the corpus are not the US retail calendar: Noche Buena, Soup Joumou and Three Kings in Miami, Navidad a Reyes in Boricua Orlando, Orthodox Christmas for Denver's Serbian fans, Lunar New Year in the Bay, Brooklyn and Toronto, Diwali and Carnival in Toronto, Ramadan and Eid in Dearborn, and Fiesta in San Antonio. Briefs repeatedly warn that these communities want to co-design, not receive a translated tee.
themes.implication: Extend holiday allocation and gift boxes from Black Friday through Jan 7 in these markets, write product Spanish-first or Kreyol-first where the community leads, and sign co-designers a season ahead so 2027 heritage capsules are authored, not adapted.

themes.title: In the sign-painting markets, lettering is the product
themes.insight: Hand lettering is the shared design language of Memphis, LA's rotulos and serigraphs, San Antonio's West Side, Houston's pinstripers and multilingual sign painters, Orlando's OBT signage, Phoenix's Van Buren neon and New Orleans' hand-painted craft. In these seven markets the letterform itself carries the local identity, so a generic Nike font on a team color reads as an outsider's product.
themes.implication: Commission a named local letterer per market to draw the wordmarks, numerals and Codes-template type for that city, and print them on in-line blanks through the quick-turn lane; the payment and credit terms follow the league co-author model in the Portland principles rather than a separate deal.

themes.title: Price lines are written by tax codes and family size
themes.insight: The retail dossiers set hard ceilings from local rules and households: New York's $110 clothing exemption, Massachusetts' $175 line, Texas's under-$100 tax-free weekend, Oklahoma's sub-$100 statewide buyer, Memphis's $35-$50 tee, and Utah, Sacramento, San Antonio and the Clippers buying for families of four or five through youth jerseys first.
themes.implication: Ladder every market's assortment against its own tax line and family math: a hero hoodie under $110 in New York, swingmans and jackets under $175 in Massachusetts, sub-$100 sets for Texas and Oklahoma, and youth-first jersey depth with family-pack tees in the statewide and rebuild markets.

clusters.name: Heirloom Dynasties
clusters.description: The league's global heritage brands (18 banners, six banners, 17 Lakers titles, the Knicks' 1973-to-2026 bookend, the Warriors' four-title run) where fandom is inherited like a family crest, tourists and global fans add volume, and the roster is judged against the lineage. Four of the five wear Specter this season.
clusters.playbook: Let heritage and the uniform system carry national volume (ring night, Specter, banners, Showtime, the Bay Bridge logo) and put creative risk in the neighborhoods rather than the skyline: borough and area-code doors in New York, Eastside serigraphs in LA, Roxbury and Dorchester in Boston, Madison Street in Chicago, Oakland first in the Bay. Launch in the neighborhood door the same day as the arena, keep core uniforms untouched, and use Christmas and playoff nights as the global stages.

clusters.name: Diaspora Metros
clusters.description: Big, diaspora-majority metros holding a new star or a playoff roster (Giannis in Miami, LeBron and Brown in Philadelphia, Leonard in Toronto, Wembanyama in San Antonio, Durant and Sengun in Houston) where the jersey wall moves the volume and multilingual community calendars provide the depth. The cluster is defined by community calendars, not standings: Detroit, Oklahoma City and Cleveland contend from other clusters.
clusters.playbook: Stock deep at the opener and through the holidays in every size and tier, keep the hyper-local pieces for earned moments (wins, playoff rounds, Fiesta, White Hot nights), and build each community's capsule with that community on its own calendar: Cuban, Haitian and Venezuelan Miami, North Fifth Street Philly, Toronto's Diwali-to-Carnival year, San Antonio's West Side, Southwest Houston. Pre-produce playoff fast-turn kits with local printers because these markets are likely to play into May.

clusters.name: Great Lakes Shift Workers
clusters.description: Cold, blue-collar, earned-trust markets (the 313, the 216 and 330, Cream City, 92 county gyms) whose fans prize effort over flash, punish hype and outsider pity, and buy heavyweight layers through a suburban mall ring.
clusters.playbook: Talk like a shift, not a scoreboard: grit-over-polish graphics in stencil, gig-poster ink and steel, heavyweight fleece and shells as the hero, and rolling rosters of paid local makers so product reads as made here rather than Portland's idea of the Rust Belt. Price for value, distribute along I-94, I-75 and the outlet corridors, and time drops to December gifting, MLK Day and the playoff run rather than the Lions, Browns or Colts fall.

clusters.name: Statewide Loyalists
clusters.description: Markets whose fan base is an entire state or region (Oklahoma, Utah, Colorado, Minnesota, Oregon, the Sacramento Valley) even where other major-league teams share the market; only Oklahoma City is a true one-team state. They are loyal, family-sized, value-minded and allergic to hype or condescension, and they split into contenders running a value ladder (Oklahoma City, Denver, Minnesota) and rebuilds selling identity (Utah, Sacramento), with Portland in between.
clusters.playbook: Sell the state, not the skyline: state-outline and multi-area-code lines, youth-first jersey ladders and family packs, distributed through big-box, mall and highway-corridor pop-ups (I-15 Saturdays, I-5 regional doors). In the contenders, run the value ladder alongside deep player stock and playoff fast-turn (Loud City, Jokic moments, Edwards-Ball); in the rebuilds, lead with identity and family gifting. Use a few credited artist drops from the city's taste districts for credibility, take climate cues from the layer and Sun Belt themes market by market, and use Portland as the home lab for this cluster's playbook.

clusters.name: City-Before-Crest Culture Capitals
clusters.description: Black-led design capitals (go-go DC, hip-hop Atlanta, brass-band New Orleans, Memphis rap and jookin) where the city's own culture runs far hotter than the team's fandom, which arrives in spikes after rebuilds or losing seasons.
clusters.playbook: Plan roughly two-thirds city-first product carrying a secondary team mark and one-third player and team product, drop on the city's own dates (404 Day, Mardi Gras, MLK Day, Labor Day, second-line Sundays) rather than national windows, and lead every program with paid institutions and creators who own the culture (go-go bands, AUC, brass bands, Memphis rap artists, Caribbean Brooklyn). Hold uniform ideas for 2027-28 and later, after partners have co-authored them.

clusters.name: Sun Belt Arrival Cities
clusters.description: Sprawling, car-bound, transplant and Latino-heavy Sun Belt metros (Orlando, Phoenix, Dallas, Charlotte) with prove-it or reset rosters, little national TV, a tourist-or-souvenir shopper next to the local one, and a heat-inverted calendar.
clusters.playbook: Separate the local from the souvenir: locals-only identity drops (407, Los Suns, Desde la Cliff, 704) next to a simple wordmark lane for visitors. Launch where taste is set (Oak Cliff, Roosevelt Row, Parramore, NoDa and the West End) and cascade value-tiered volume to suburban malls and outlets. Lead with Nike-owned heritage where it exists (Penny pinstripes, the Hive) and build Spanish-first co-design programs for Hispanic Heritage Month 2027.

clusters.name: Second Team in a Two-Team Town
clusters.description: The Clippers and the Nets share a media market with a bigger, older brand (the Lakers, the champion Knicks), so their fans define themselves by neighborhood and by not being the other team. Both have the league's thinnest fandom this season (a starless Clippers reset, a 20-62 Nets rebuild) but real footprints: Inglewood, the South Bay, Long Beach and the SGV; Brooklyn's Caribbean, Black and Asian neighborhoods.
clusters.playbook: Design for the footprint, not the metro: Inglewood sign letters, the six LA codes and South Bay Filipino and Pacific Islander hoops for the Clippers; Kings County, Caribbean Brooklyn and Sunset Park for the Nets. Never mock the big brother; win the shared nights instead (the Clippers' House Rules on Lakers-at-Dome nights). Keep units modest and youth-first, rework the closets left by departed stars, and hold uniform ideas for 2027-28 builds co-authored with local partners.

tentpoles.window: Oct 20-27, 2026 (opening night Oct 20 on NBC; opening week)
tentpoles.moment: Opening night tripleheader and opening week: Boston at Detroit, Philadelphia at New York (Knicks ring night), Oklahoma City at San Antonio (West finals rematch)
tentpoles.play: Nationally, lead with the champion's ring night and the new-look Sixers, both in Specter-era storytelling. Locally, 'Clock In' graphics in Detroit, the 1973/2026 rafter tee in New York, 'Built Here' and the returning Fiesta-stripe City Edition in Oklahoma City and San Antonio, plus opening-week jersey-wall restocks for the Luka era in LA, Flagg in Dallas and the whole-roster Lillard-Morant wall in Portland. Cleveland's 'gratitude, then the Cavs' LeBron beat runs at the Sixers' home opener against the Cavaliers (date to confirm) and their East Group B Cup meeting, not in January.

tentpoles.window: Oct 30-Nov 27, 2026 group play (Fridays plus Tue Nov 24 and Wed Nov 25), quarterfinals Dec 4-5, home semifinals Dec 8-9, final Dec 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse
tentpoles.moment: Emirates NBA Cup: two home Cup nights per market, then the first knockouts outside Las Vegas
tentpoles.play: Each team plays four group games and only two at home, so every market gets two home-Cup drops mapped to its own dates (Oct 30 home teams: Washington, Indiana, Toronto, Boston, Minnesota, Phoenix, San Antonio, Utah, the Clippers and Portland; confirm the rest from each schedule), and the national 'Cup Nights' story is stitched weekly from whichever markets are home that night: Atlanta's Pac-Man heritage, the Clippers' Inglewood sign-letter launch, Milwaukee fish-fry Fridays, Denver's artist-print pilot, Oklahoma's Cup hoodie. Hold 48-hour knockout hoodies on pre-approved blanks for quarterfinal and home-semifinal markets (Minnesota's ready-swap pipeline is the template), and make Hinkle the national Dec 11 story of Indiana as the home of the game, with or without the Pacers: a maple-and-navy 'Fieldhouse Winter' layer and a 92-county 'Sectional' tee.

tentpoles.window: Select 2026-27 games, dates to be announced (collection on sale since the Sept 9 reveal)
tentpoles.moment: Specter nights: the first Specter game in each of the eight heritage markets
tentpoles.play: Run one league-wide Specter rollout keyed to each club's first Specter game once the schedule is known: a national 'heritage, re-cut' story with a local layer in each of the eight markets. Sacramento and Atlanta, which have few other national hooks, get full local programs: Sacramento puts Specter at the front of the team store and DOCO with a licensed Arco-era tee beside it, and Atlanta pairs it with its red-and-gold and Pac-Man heritage on home nights. In Boston, Los Angeles, Golden State, New York, Philadelphia and Detroit it rides alongside ring night, Christmas and the opener.

tentpoles.window: Nov 27, 2026 (Black Friday) to Jan 7, 2027 (Orthodox Christmas), with Noche Buena Dec 24, Soup Joumou Jan 1 and Three Kings Jan 6
tentpoles.moment: The plural holiday: US gifting plus diaspora gift calendars
tentpoles.play: Nationally, youth jersey gift boxes and family bundles. Locally, extend allocation and storytelling to the community's own date: Cuban, Haitian and Latin gift sets in Miami, Navidad a Reyes boxes in Orlando, Orthodox Christmas Jokic gifting in Denver, Valley gift ladders in Sacramento and Utah, and Mexican-American family packs from Oak Cliff and San Antonio.

tentpoles.moment: Christmas Day: Spurs at Knicks (Finals rematch), Heat at Celtics, 76ers at Lakers (LeBron's return), Thunder at Timberwolves, Nuggets at Warriors
tentpoles.play: The national play is the five-game showcase with the champion at noon. Locally: the Game 4 'Back Page' gift box in New York, a Giannis-Heat vs. Boston rivalry tee, a Lakers 'thank-you, then the new era' watch-party program, Mill City Christmas in Minneapolis, and a Christmas-night crab-feed poster tee in the Bay.

tentpoles.window: Jan 18, 2027 (NBC/Peacock MLK Day quadrupleheader), with programs running MLK week through February
tentpoles.moment: MLK Day: Pistons at Cavaliers, 76ers at Hawks, Timberwolves at Knicks, Rockets vs. Grizzlies, and the start of Black History Month programs league-wide
tentpoles.play: Lead with community funding and access, not product: Atlanta's Beloved Community program, a Karamu House capsule in Cleveland, Memphis's partner program near the National Civil Rights Museum, Third Ward heritage in Houston. February then carries co-authored Black history capsules: Russell's Boston, Brooklyn Firsts, West End Charlotte, Harlem's Rens, Chicago's AfriCOBRA lineage, DC go-go and Albina in Portland.

tentpoles.window: Jan 21 (Brown's first return to TD Garden), Jan 28 (Giannis returns to Milwaukee, after the Nov 18 first meeting in Miami), Feb 15 (Ball returns to Charlotte), plus Portland vs. Memphis and Toronto vs. the Clippers (dates to confirm)
tentpoles.play: Nationally these are the season's most-watched storylines. Locally, sell the city and gratitude, never the departed star: Milwaukee's 'Champions City' 2021 piece, a Boston-Philadelphia rivalry archive, Charlotte's new-core night for Miller and Knueppel, and 'thank you, city' pieces for Memphis and the Clippers on their Morant and Leonard nights, with Portland and Toronto selling the welcome. Cleveland's LeBron beat sits in October-November with the opener.

tentpoles.window: Feb 6, 2027 (Lunar New Year, Year of the Goat) and Feb 9, 2027 (Mardi Gras; king cake season from Jan 6)
tentpoles.moment: Lunar New Year and Carnival season
tentpoles.play: Partner-designed Year of the Goat pieces where Asian American fans are core business, not a theme night (the Bay, Brooklyn's Sunset Park, Toronto, Flushing, Koreatown LA, Sacramento), and New Orleans' Twelfth Night pack timed to king cake rather than tourist purple-green-gold.

tentpoles.window: Feb 15, 2027 (Presidents' Day quadrupleheader) to Feb 19-21, 2027 (All-Star Weekend, Phoenix)
tentpoles.play: The national All-Star story is told from Phoenix street level: a locals-first 'Made on Roosevelt' pop-up with Valley artists, Booker-led volume, Los Suns and the Mercury's women's line. Other markets localize with home watch parties and 'our All-Star' tees on in-line blanks for their selected players, and hold trade-deadline (Feb 11) quick-turn slots for any arriving player.

tentpoles.window: Apr 4 (404 Day), Apr 7 (407 Day), Apr 14 (414 Day, confirm local recognition), late April Fiesta San Antonio (confirm 2027 dates), then the Play-In Apr 13-16
tentpoles.moment: Spring city days: area-code days and Fiesta
tentpoles.play: Use local identity days as the spring bridge into the playoffs: Atlanta's 404 Day chapter of the area-code capsule, Orlando's locals-only 407 Day drop, a Milwaukee 414 drop if local partners confirm the day, and San Antonio's Fiesta-stripe drop with medal-pin caps. Other markets' code days land on their own dates from the Codes calendar (313 Day Mar 13 in Detroit, 216 Day Feb 16 in Cleveland, 504 Day May 4 in New Orleans), not in this window.

tentpoles.window: Apr 17 or 18, 2027 (playoffs begin; confirm) through the June Finals
tentpoles.play: Nationally, round tees and caps. Locally, pre-approved 48-hour clinch kits printed by local licensed printers in each contender: Loud City blue-outs, White Hot Linen, Overtime in Detroit, Unfinished Business in Cleveland, Clutch City red-outs, Rip City red, Knicks maker-series playoff tees and a Fiesta-plus-playoffs stripe in San Antonio.

tentpoles.window: Jun 5, 2027 ('77-at-50) and Juneteenth (Jun 19), alongside the Finals and the draft (late June, confirm)
tentpoles.moment: Portland's 1977 title at 50, Juneteenth and Pride
tentpoles.play: Portland's '77-at-50 archive-exact reissue by raffle, co-authored with Albina, is the one heritage moment Nike can tell from its own hometown. Juneteenth pieces in Houston's Third Ward and Pride capsules co-made with local partners (Brooklyn with the Liberty, Toronto's Blockorama) run alongside.

tentpoles.window: July to August 2027: park circuits, Kobe Day (Aug 24) and back-to-school tax-free weekends (confirm state dates)
tentpoles.play: Nationally, a park-court performance line. Locally, the summer leagues and courts each market already owns: Rucker and Dyckman in New York, the Drew in LA, Goodman League in DC, BNBL in Boston, Miami's park courts, Eastlake night courts in Phoenix, Irving Park in Portland. Ship Sun Belt youth packs before the Texas and Florida tax-free weekends, and run the 8/24 muralist series as a separate, estate-approved Kobe calendar.

tentpoles.window: Sep 15 to Oct 15, 2027 (Hispanic Heritage Month) and October 2027 (Filipino American History Month), running into the 2027-28 City Edition season
tentpoles.moment: Heritage months and the 2027-28 launch window
tentpoles.play: Launch the co-designed capsules signed this season: Hecho en el 407, Los Suns club jacket, Summer Avenue in Memphis, Westside Denver, Desde la Cliff's 2027 build, Ube x Mango in LA and the Bay's Filipino heritage line, then roll straight into the 2027-28 City Edition pitches (Brooklyn's Kings County, Chicago's 1901 W. Madison, Minnesota's Mill City Lights).

priorities.title: Banner '26: the 1973 bookend, ring night to Christmas (ring-night-1973-2026)
priorities.why: The league's biggest market defends its first title in 53 years with ring night on opening night and the Finals rematch at noon on Christmas, the two highest-visibility dates of the season, and the 1973/2026 story is one only Nike-dressed New York can tell. Rank key 99 (opportunity 94 + 5 for opening night and Christmas at home).

priorities.title: Next Chapter: win the jersey wall at the opener (next-chapter-opener)
priorities.why: The NBA's most mythologized brand is resetting its jersey wall around Doncic and Reaves with no visual identity yet claimed, in a market where every retail tier already exists, so the opener sets the era's look and volume for years. Rank key 95 (opportunity 90 + 5 for a Christmas home game).

priorities.title: Earn Philly: stock the debut, unlock the welcome (earn-philly-home-debut)
priorities.why: A LeBron and Brown superteam in a Specter season is the league's biggest new-arrival opening, and Philadelphia's earn-it unlock mechanic is the template for every arrival market. Rank key 86 (opportunity 86).

priorities.title: Giannis arrival season, built on what exists (giannis-305-arrival)
priorities.why: Giannis, confirmed in Miami by the live-verified League Pulse, is the biggest Nike signature star in Heat colors this era, arriving in a title-or-bust year in a gateway shopping market, and the brief's plan ships now on existing Freak colorways and swingman depth. Rank key 86 (opportunity 86).

priorities.title: Wembanyama youth ladder and sub-$100 tier (wemby-youth-ladder)
priorities.why: A title co-favorite with a Nike global star in a family-sized, price-aware region that runs to Mexico makes always-on youth depth the highest-volume, lowest-risk bet in the West. Rank key 85 (opportunity 80 + 5 for the opening-night home game).

priorities.title: Blazermania 50: the '77-at-50 line, sequenced to rights (blazermania-50)
priorities.why: A once-only anniversary in Nike's hometown with an empty City Edition slot, and the home-lab market where the Albina co-author model and the rights-sequenced heritage calendar get proven before they roll out league-wide. Rank key 76 (opportunity 66 + 10 for a once-only '77-at-50 date in Nike's hometown).

priorities.title: Shift Change: the winter layer program (shift-change-winter)
priorities.why: A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year with a seven-month outerwear season makes Detroit the strongest contender-plus-winter combination, provided the product speaks its own knit and shell language rather than Carhartt's. Rank key 73 (opportunity 68 + 5 for the opening-night home game).

priorities.title: Made on Roosevelt: the locals-first All-Star pop-up (all-star-made-on-roosevelt)
priorities.why: All-Star Weekend is the league's one fixed national stage in a single market, and a locals-first pop-up that clears licensing in time sets the template for how Nike shows up at every future All-Star. Rank key 72 (opportunity 62 + 10 for hosting All-Star).

priorities.title: Raptors Winter Blackout, sold coast to coast (winter-blackout-north)
priorities.why: Canada's only team sells to a whole country through a five-month winter, and the layer program is the largest single cold-weather opportunity in the league while staying clear of the anti-US mood that hampers loud campaigns. Rank key 72 (opportunity 72).

priorities.title: Cup Fridays into holiday gifting (holiday-and-cup)
priorities.why: A 60.5-win-total co-favorite whose star is a Converse athlete and whose fan base is a whole state buying under $100 for families, so Gilgeous-Alexander, Williams and Holmgren youth jerseys and state-outline gifts are the efficient volume play through Cup nights and the holidays. Rank key 70 (opportunity 70).

priorities.title: Nor'easter layering system with a snow-emergency drop (noreaster-layering)
priorities.why: Elite loyalty and high-income New England retail meet a $175 tax-free clothing line and a five-month winter, and layers sidestep the roster doubt that caps player product after the Brown trade. Rank key 69 (opportunity 64 + 5 for a Christmas home game).

priorities.title: Lake Wind: the coat over the jersey (lake-wind-outerwear)
priorities.why: Chicago's global heritage retail engine is already in place, so the cold-weather hero coat is the biggest net-new revenue line in a rebuild year and the anchor of the 2027-28 Big Shoulders build. Rank key 66 (opportunity 66).

priorities.title: Mill City Christmas for the OKC home game (mill-city-christmas)
priorities.why: Minnesota hosts the Thunder on Christmas night, anchors the Cup ready-swap template and sits in more league tentpoles than any market without a board item, and a Mill City holiday layer sells the city while both stars wear rival brands. Rank key 63 (opportunity 58 + 5 for a Christmas home game).

priorities.title: Clutch Red and Gold heritage line (red-and-gold-clutch-heritage)
priorities.why: The reported 2026-27 red-and-gold throwback (verify) would unlock the 1971-95 memory in a 47.5-win-total market with one of the league's most complete design languages, at lower rights risk than the slab-finish capsule; the item is gated on confirmation of the Classic/throwback designation and Olajuwon likeness clearance. Rank key 60 (opportunity 60).

priorities.title: 404 / 678 / 770 metro capsule, with a 404 Day chapter (area-code-metro-capsule)
priorities.why: Atlanta is the cleanest proof of the 'city before crest' theme, with near-top culture and soft team fandom, and its area-code capsule is the prototype for the league-wide Codes template. Rank key 59 (opportunity 54 + 5 for its MLK Day home game).

portland.title: Travel in three sweeps keyed to the calendar, not 30 visits
portland.detail: Sweep one (re-baselined to Oct 9-Nov 27, opener plus Cup) covers only markets with this-season decoration on in-line blanks (New York, Philadelphia, Los Angeles, Miami, San Antonio, Oklahoma City, Detroit, Portland and the Cup home markets), sweep two (MLK Day Jan 18 to All-Star Feb 19-21) covers civic, Specter and heritage programs, and sweep three (May to July) runs 2027-28 co-design sessions. Each sweep has a named owner pair (the Portland market lead plus the regional partner manager), a fixed market list, a travel budget set as a share of the season activation budget (roughly 40/35/25 across the three sweeps) and a go/no-go checklist: signed partner agreement, rights cleared, blank stock on hand and a licensed printer slotted. Between sweeps, local partners and licensed printers handle fast-turn so nobody flies product to a clinch.

portland.title: Run two product clocks and say which one every idea is on
portland.detail: Cut-and-sew, footwear colorways and City Edition pitches sit on a 9-18 month clock, so most 2026-27 briefs correctly hold uniforms for 2027-28 or 2028-29; anything for this season must be decoration on in-line blanks through a 2-6 week quick-turn lane. Every market plan should tag each product 'ships now', 'FW27' or 'uniform cycle' before it reaches a review.

portland.title: One partner model, 30 local casts
portland.detail: Use a standard paid co-author agreement (fee plus royalty, credit on the hangtag, approval rights, multi-year term) and a 'listen first' season where the briefs ask for it (Caribbean Brooklyn, Minnesota's Somali, Hmong and Native communities, Denver's Welton Street and Westside, Albina). Pair it with a central rights desk for Converse, Jordan, NBPA, school, HBCU and estate approvals, since a third of the top opportunities are gated on clearance.

portland.title: Use Portland as the lab, not the template
portland.detail: Pilot the Albina co-author model, the Big Dark layer program and the 48-hour clinch kit with Portland Gear at home first, using the most Nike-literate crowd in the league as a wear-test and credibility panel. Do not export Portland's insider taste to value-led markets like Oklahoma, Utah or Memphis, where the same system needs simpler graphics and sub-$100 price ladders.

portland.title: Resource by calibrated tiers, not by market size alone
portland.detail: Tier 1 (league opportunity 75 or higher: New York, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami, Philadelphia, San Antonio) gets full national programs and about 45% of the activation budget; Tier 2 (55-74: Toronto, Oklahoma City, Detroit, Portland, Chicago, Boston, Phoenix, Houston, Minnesota) gets about 35%, with Oklahoma City run as a contender on a value ladder rather than a small market; Tier 3 (below 55) gets about 20%, split between craft-led culture capitals (New Orleans, Atlanta, Brooklyn, DC, Memphis) and value programs (Utah, Sacramento, Indiana, Milwaukee, Charlotte). Re-score every market at the Feb 11 trade deadline and after the first round, because the reshuffle showed how fast a face can move.

portland.title: Read league scores as calibrated and brief scores as local
portland.detail: Each brief scores its market on its own terms; the league scores re-calibrate all 30 against each other (about 50 = league average on opportunity, retail and fandom; culture runs higher, median about 62, because every brief rated its own design well highly), stay within 25 points of the brief, and every score note quotes the brief's numbers so the two can be read side by side. Culture scores only the depth of distinct local design material; brand crowding and door quality belong to retail, and opportunity is demand plus Nike's rights position. The priority board ranks by opportunity plus a date bonus (+10 for a once-only date Nike can own in the market, +5 for an opening-night, Christmas or MLK Day home game); below the cut are Golden State (59), Indiana (58, whose Hinkle final is carried by the Cup tentpole), Cleveland (55) and Denver (48).

watchlist.why: Verified in the league calendar: on Mar 25, 2026 the Board of Governors voted 30-0 to explore expansion bids from Seattle and Las Vegas for a 2028-29 entry, with reported fees of $7-10B per team; a final vote needs 23 of 30 governors and no franchise has been awarded, and Adam Silver repeated in September that he aims to decide by the end of 2026. Seattle lost the SuperSonics to Oklahoma City in 2008 and keeps their green and gold alive through nostalgia and the Storm, three hours from Portland. Dated trigger: by the end-of-2026 decision, Portland should have a Sonics-heritage contingency plan ready (mark rights, Storm and local partners, and careful handling of Oklahoma City's origin story).

The other bid in the verified 30-0 exploratory vote (2028-29 target, $7-10B fees, decision expected by the end of 2026, with reports that Las Vegas may be decided before Seattle). It already hosts Summer League, the Aces and three NBA Cup finals (2023-25) before the 2026 final moved to Hinkle; the fan base would be built from transplants and tourists, closest to the Sun Belt Arrival Cities cluster. Confirm the ownership group and arena plan once an award is made.

The league has staged regular-season games there and runs the G League's Capitanes, and San Antonio's 'Spurs Nation' and the Mavericks' and Suns' Latino bases already reach across the border. Confirm 2026-27 Mexico City games and any NBA Europe or international expansion news before planning a Spanish-first regional line.

watchlist.market: Portland (Moda Center lease) and the Clippers (Aspiration ruling)
watchlist.why: Two existing markets in flux: Portland has $586M in public commitments toward Moda Center upgrades but no signed lease under new owner Tom Dundon, and the Clippers play this season with Steve Ballmer suspended for a year, a $30M fine and their 2029-2033 first-round picks taken (Sept 2 ruling, confirmed in the live-verified League Pulse; appeals or changes not tracked). Confirm the lease status and the Clippers' business-side leadership before committing multi-year partner money in either; the Clippers' league scores do not depend on the ruling.

scores.note: The league ceiling on opportunity, culture and fandom: the biggest market defending its first title since 1973 with the deepest homegrown basketball, music and art culture, while retail sits just behind the Lakers and Chicago because MSG, Puma's Clyde and Fanatics crowd Nike's lane in the most license-heavy market (brief scores: opportunity 91, culture 96, retail 84, fandom 94).

Second only to New York on opportunity and first on retail because a reset jersey wall in the league's most mythologized brand meets every retail tier, while fandom sits below the true elite this season on grief over LeBron and a 46.5-win projection (brief scores: opportunity 90, culture 94, retail 88, fandom 86).

Top-three opportunity because Giannis is Nike's biggest signature star in a gateway shopping market with deep Cuban, Haitian and Latin design material, but fandom is just above average because Miami's crowd is playoff-and-winning driven rather than lifer-loyal (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 72).

A LeBron-and-Brown contender in a Specter year gives Philadelphia top-four opportunity and elite-adjacent fandom; its design material (Philly soul, the mural program, North Fifth Street, Iverson-era street style) is real but less distinct than the top culture band, and retail is held down by thin taste-setting independents and a throwback lane owned by Mitchell & Ness (brief scores: opportunity 86, culture 91, retail 68, fandom 85).

A title co-favorite led by Wembanyama in a one-team region that runs to Mexico puts fandom and opportunity near the top, while retail is ordinary mall-and-Academy volume and its Fiesta and West Side culture is distinctive but narrower than the coastal giants' (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 86, retail 56, fandom 90).

A country-sized market with the Leonard reunion and Nike's own Carter archive sits above average everywhere, held below the US giants by CAD pricing, cross-border leakage and post-'Elbows Up' wariness of US brands (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 88, retail 70, fandom 80).

The league's second-most intense fandom and a 60.5-win co-favorite with a Converse-signed star put opportunity in the top ten (scored on demand and Nike's rights position, not doors), while small-metro, value-minded retail and a thinner design well than the culture capitals keep retail and culture below average (brief scores: opportunity 70, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 86).

A 60-win No. 1 seed in a Specter year with a seven-month outerwear season and a deep maker culture lifts opportunity, culture and fandom well above average, while a thin city-core retail map and unconfirmed partner doors keep retail below the line (brief scores: opportunity 80, culture 90, retail 55, fandom 80).

The six-banner heritage engine and a full flagship-to-mall network put Chicago's retail second in the league and culture in the top five, but a 31-51 rebuild and a 2027-28 build window hold opportunity and fandom nearer the middle (brief scores: opportunity 82, culture 93, retail 84, fandom 74).

Nike's hometown, a once-only '77-at-50 year, a Lillard-Morant backcourt and intense statewide loyalty lift opportunity and fandom well above average, while few public Nike doors and a Rose Quarter retail desert put retail below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 56, fandom 80).

Elite heritage fandom and strong New England retail, but roster doubt after the Brown trade and Nike playing away to New Balance and adidas cap opportunity, and its design well is narrower than the Black-led design capitals' (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 84, retail 78, fandom 86).

Hosting All-Star (Feb 19-21) and an under-served Latino base lift opportunity above average; the Valley's Chicano, Indigenous and Van Buren neon material puts culture just below the league median, retail is around average, and a bubble roster holds fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 78, culture 82, retail 62, fandom 64).

One of the most complete local design languages in the league and a Durant-Sengun playoff team keep culture high and opportunity above average, but car-bound sprawl and a football-Astros-rodeo attention war keep retail near average and fandom below it (brief scores: opportunity 76, culture 90, retail 62, fandom 64).

A loud Edwards-Ball team with a Christmas home game, Garnett's retirement and a deep Minneapolis Sound, Mill City and Somali, Hmong and Native design well put opportunity, culture and fandom above average, but both stars wear rival brands and retail is suburban-mall led (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 84, retail 58, fandom 76).

One of the league's deepest design wells sits on one of its softest fan bases, because Atlanta's pride runs to the city rather than the Hawks, so culture is top-five while fandom sits in the bottom quarter (brief scores: opportunity 74, culture 92, retail 64, fandom 52).

Oakland, San Francisco and Asian American lineages put the Bay's design well in the league's top band and its spending keeps retail high, but a 40.5-win total and an open Curry shoe deal hold opportunity and fandom at the league middle (brief scores: opportunity 72, culture 92, retail 78, fandom 70).

Title-or-bust loyalty puts fandom above average and its punk, rap, steel and Akron material sits below the league median, but a drive-to-the-mall retail map with no sneaker district and a Browns-first fall keep retail below the line and opportunity at it (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 76, retail 48, fandom 72).

A three-time MVP, a 49.5-win total and a long outerwear season keep opportunity close to the pack, but a quiet, understated base, an edge-of-metro retail map and a narrower design well than most put Denver just below average (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 68, retail 48, fandom 64).

A Hinkle Cup final and Haliburton's return give a small market near-average opportunity and above-average gym-faith fandom, while value-led, mall-first retail with no destination door sits in the bottom tier (brief scores: opportunity 68, culture 76, retail 45, fandom 72).

Brooklyn's borough culture and New York retail rank high, but after 20-62 in a Knicks title year Nets fandom is the league's second-thinnest and the real opportunity is a 2027 build (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 92, retail 72, fandom 40).

DC's go-go, flag and ward culture sits in the league's top third, but a 17-65 hangover in a hockey-first, visiting-fan-heavy arena gives it the fourth-softest fandom until Dybantsa proves out (brief scores: opportunity 66, culture 90, retail 58, fandom 44).

A huge metro with Flagg and distinct Oak Cliff and Fair Park languages has average retail scale and design material below the median, but a wounded 26-56 fan base and football's grip on the fall put opportunity and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 70, retail 58, fandom 54).

Memphis's design well (soul, living rap, jookin, sign painting) is in the league's top third, but a post-Ja reset in a small, price-conscious metro with no Nike door puts retail second from the bottom (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 88, retail 38, fandom 66).

Penny pinstripes and a large Boricua base give Orlando a real lane and design material below the median, but no national stage, outlet-heavy retail and playoff-gated loyalty keep opportunity, retail and fandom in the bottom half (brief scores: opportunity 64, culture 72, retail 58, fandom 56).

The Inglewood-to-SGV footprint gives the Clippers real design material below the league median and LA retail keeps retail above average, but a starless post-Kawhi reset in the Lakers' shadow gives them the league's third-thinnest fandom and a low opportunity, a score that holds with or without the Aspiration penalties (brief scores: opportunity 60, culture 80, retail 72, fandom 41).

Hive nostalgia is real, but non-Nike faces, one national window and a college-first, mall-and-outlet metro put Charlotte in the bottom fifth on opportunity and fandom and below average on culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 58, culture 66, retail 52, fandom 50).

Whole-state, family-sized loyalty keeps fandom near the league average, but a small metro in a rebuild with no national stage and a thin boutique layer sits near the bottom on opportunity, culture and retail (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 66, retail 40, fandom 68).

Fans who saved the team keep fandom just above average, but a likely bottom-West season, a value-leaning Valley and a lighter design well than its California neighbors put Sacramento near the floor on the other three axes, with Specter its main national hook (brief scores: opportunity 52, culture 63, retail 44, fandom 70).

Life after Giannis in a small, value-minded rebuild gives Milwaukee the league's second-lowest opportunity, with Cream City brick and fish-fry Fridays as its main design assets and fandom below average until Jan 28 (brief scores: opportunity 50, culture 70, retail 40, fandom 56).

The starkest split in the league: New Orleans's culture is second only to New York's, but thin retail, a Saints-first city and a 26-56 team put opportunity, retail and fandom at the floor, so it is a craft market, not a volume market (brief scores: opportunity 46, culture 96, retail 34, fandom 38).
